title: Saffron Technologies - renewal & geo extension sync
summary: Quarterly renewal check-in focused on bumping committed capacity, adding APAC region, and clarifying private/VPC deployment options and security needs. Agreed to run a 48-hour throughput/latency benchmark on Redwood Dedicated in eu-west then mirror to apac, and Redwood to send an updated quote & SOC2 + KMS docs.
topics: security: SOC 2, KMS and audit logs
action_items: Maya Chen - Send updated 12-month quote with APAC add-on and burst bucket breakdown - 2025-06-03
Omar Patel - Share benchmark runbook and baseline perf sheet, include KV cache notes - 2025-06-02
Priya Singh - Provide internal PKI and KMS contact info + requirements - 2025-06-05
next_steps: Redwood to provision a small Dedicated pool for 48-hour test (eu-west) and share S3 upload for traces
Schedule SE deep-dive for private/VPC network design (week of 6/9)
Send legal term amendment draft for 12-month extension with regional addendum
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-05-29 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Park (CTO - Saffron), Diego Ramos (Head of ML), Priya Singh (SRE)

Summary auto-generated: Quick renewal/expansion sync. Focus on committed tokens increase from 120M -> 200M/mo, APAC region onramp and private VPC discussion.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. Quick roll-call?
[00:05] Lena Park: Hey, Lena here. Diego and Priya on my side, thanks.
[00:08] Diego Ramos: Hey all.
[00:10] Priya Singh: Priya here.
[00:12] Maya Chen: Cool. We put together a tentative uplift proposal — Omar will walk the perf bits — but first, high level what's changed since our last check?
[00:20] Lena Park: Timeline moved up a bit — we want APAC live ahead of the Q4 campaign. Also we've seen a ton more embed/semantic search traffic so our token burn is spikier than predicted, the 120M won't cut it.
[00:30] Diego Ramos: Yeah we're seeing 2-3x peak bursts, and p95 token latency needs to be <120ms for user flows. Right now eu-west is okay but we need apac to be comparable.
[00:44] Omar Patel: Understood. For the Dedicated tier we can provision a regional pool in apac-northeast within two weeks once contracts are signed, there's a short lead for GPUs but we can prioritize a small pool for the pilot. On perf, the KV cache and prefix caching help a lot for repeated contexts — that's probably why your p50 is good but p95 is spiking on cold starts.
[01:05] Priya Singh: Quick Q — our security team asked whether Redwood Private (the VPC package) supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs that tie into our Splunk. Is that in scope?
[01:15] Omar Patel: Yes, Private supports KMS integration; we can integrate with your cloud KMS or HSM. Audit logs are exported via secure S3 and can stream to SIEMs — though the initial connector might need a small mapping job. I'll share the integration doc.
[01:28] Lena Park: And SOC 2? We need current attestations for legal.
[01:32] Maya Chen: We are SOC 2 Type II certed, I'll attach the latest report. Also we can provide us-east data flows and a regional addendum in the amendment.
[01:40] Diego Ramos: Cost question — if we go Dedicated with APAC, are we locked into a fixed rate for the GPUs or is there a burst pool option? We want a base commit and then bursts.
[01:48] Maya Chen: We typically do a committed baseline with a burst bucket that's billed at a higher but predictable rate. For pilot we can do a temporary burst allowance. We'll put the exact numbers in the quote.
[01:57] Priya Singh: Example numbers would help — currently we're spending ~ $32k/mo and need to cap at ~ $60k with headroom.
[02:06] Maya Chen: Ok noted. Omar, can you run an estimate for 200M tokens/mo committed with a 20% burst cap to 260M? Include both hosted and dedicated compares.
[02:15] Omar Patel: Yep, I'll do that. Also to align expectations: depending on model and quantization, cost per token varies — if you want <120ms p95 for chat style flows, we recommend the q4 quant profile on the RW-3 models and dedicated pool with continuous batching tuned.
[02:30] Diego Ramos: Wait, the RW-3 — isn't that the internal name? We called it 'redwood-3' in our notes, the vendor names keep changing.
[02:36] Omar Patel: Yeah sorry, naming slips — I'll put the model IDs in the runbook so there's no confusion.
[02:42] [02:45] -- short crosstalk --
[02:50] Lena Park: On the private/VPC side, our infra owner wants to know about IP allowlists and transit routing — we need a topology diagram before signoff.
[02:57] Omar Patel: We'll produce a network diagram for VPC peering, transit gateway options, and private link. For on-prem we also support air-gapped bundles but that'll add lead time.
[03:12] Priya Singh: Lead time estimate?
[03:14] Omar Patel: For VPC it's 1-2 weeks after we agree on config; for on-prem it's usually 6-8 weeks for packaging and validation.
[03:23] Diego Ramos: Benchmarks — can we run a 48-hour perf test with our top prompts and traces? We'd like to compare eu-west Dedicated baseline -> apac pilot.
[03:31] Maya Chen: Absolutely. Omar, outline what we need from Saffron and we'll spin up the pool for 48hrs.
[03:36] Omar Patel: We'll need example prompt set, representative concurrency (QPS), sample payload sizes (avg tokens in/out). We'll also provide a script to replay traces and a perf sheet to collect p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens.
[03:47] Priya Singh: We'll export a week of traffic and pick the top 40 prompt templates. Diego will own that.
[03:53] Diego Ramos: Yup, I'll grab the templates and send them to Omar.
[03:56] [04:00] Maya Chen: Legal stuff — we can start with a 12-month amendment to extend current terms; we'll include an APAC addendum and a private/VPC clause. Our legal team will draft and send a redline.
[04:12] Lena Park: Do you have a standard SLA for Dedicated? We're looking for 99.95% and a latency SLO for p95 token latency.
[04:20] Maya Chen: Our Dedicated SLAs are 99.95% availability for the serving layer; latency SLOs are configurable per route and we'll propose a p95 target that matches your flows.
[04:29] Diego Ramos: Any competitor caveats? We looked at StreamServe who offered a lower entry price but no KV cache optimization and the support model was thin. VeloxAI had lower-latency claims but required re-architecting our prompt stack.
[04:42] Omar Patel: Right — platform differences matter. We'll include a short comparison in the materials.
[04:48] [05:00] -- 10 minute mark summary -- Maya Chen: To recap: Saffron wants 200M tokens commit, APAC pilot, private/VPC options evaluated, a 48-hour perf run, and an updated quote + legal amendment. Action owners: Maya (quote & SOC2), Omar (runbook + network diagrams), Diego/Priya (prompts + infra contacts).
[05:20] Priya Singh: Small note — our security wants encryption-in-transit details between Redwood control plane and regional serving nodes; is that TLS mutual?
[05:28] Omar Patel: Yes mutual TLS between agents, and you can request a dedicated VPN tunnel for private customers. We'll capture exact cipher suites in the security pack.
[05:36] Lena Park: Any blockers for approvals on our side? Execs need the cost baseline and timeline. If that lands this week, we can sign next week.
[05:44] Maya Chen: We'll prioritize the quote and attach the SOC 2 and KMS integration doc.
[05:48] [06:00] Diego Ramos: One more technical — latency: if we enable prefix caching aggressively, does that affect freshness for dynamic prompts? We're concerned about stale user-specific context.
[06:10] Omar Patel: Good call. Prefix caching is safe for stateless prompts; for user-specific dynamic context we recommend KV caching per session with TTLs. We'll show config knobs in the runbook.
[06:22] Priya Singh: Ok. For the perf run: what's a realistic concurrency to use?
[06:26] Omar Patel: Start with your 99th percentile concurrency, but we'll also ramp to 2x to test stability. Provide us current QPS distribution and we'll script the ramp.
[06:36] Maya Chen: Anything else?
[06:40] Lena Park: If you can get the amended quote and the perf run instructions by Wednesday, we can meet the exec's ask.
[06:46] Maya Chen: We'll aim for that.
[06:48] -- End of call --

Post-call notes: Redwood to prioritize quote with explicit committed vs burst pricing, deliver SOC2 and KMS integration doc, spin up 48-hour Dedicated test in eu-west, deliver network topology/VPC diagram, schedule deep-dive week of 6/9.
